The test image shows:
- A mature soybean stem covered with prominent black specks (pycnidia) distributed along the stem surface
- Dried tan/brown pods attached to the stem
- Some whitish/gray material at nodes
- Overall late-season maturity state

The key diagnostic feature is the **black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) on the stem** — the reference image for Diaporthe confirms this pattern: black specks on stems and pods at maturity, consistent with Pod and Stem Blight. The black specks appear in organized arrangements along the stem, which distinguishes Diaporthe from Anthracnose (randomly scattered acervuli) and Charcoal Rot (microsclerotia beneath the epidermis giving a charcoal appearance internally).
